# PHOENIX-6142 Design Doc

Jira: [PHOENIX-6142](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PHOENIX-6142)  
PR: [https://github.com/apache/phoenix/pull/903](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/pull/903)

# Background

The aim of this document is to highlight the problems identified in [PHOENIX-6142](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PHOENIX-6142) (Make DDL operations resilient to orphan parent-\>child linking rows in SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK) and later discuss the proposed solution to solve these problems.

Before 4.15, "CREATE/DROP VIEW" was an atomic operation since we were issuing batch mutations on just the 1 SYSTEM.CATALOG region. In 4.15 we introduced SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK to store the parent-\>child links and so a CREATE VIEW is no longer atomic since it consists of 2 separate RPCs (1 to SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK to add the linking row and another to SYSTEM.CATALOG to write metadata for the new view).

If the second RPC i.e. the RPC to write metadata to SYSTEM.CATALOG fails after the 1st RPC has already gone through, there will be an inconsistency between both metadata tables and there will be a **parent-\>child linking row left around inside SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK. We will refer to such wrong rows as orphan linking rows** henceforth.

# How can an orphan linking row be created? {#how-can-an-orphan-linking-row-be-created?}

It is actually pretty simple to create an orphan linking row and that is what makes this problem even worse. **You can create an orphan linking row by creating a view of the same name on 2 different tables/views.** The second view creation eventually fails with a TableAlreadyExistsException, however due to the nature of the 2 RPCs explained above, the linking row for the second view is upserted into SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK anyhow. Steps to create an orphan linking row:

| CREATE TABLE T1 (TENANT\_ID VARCHAR NOT NULL, A INTEGER NOT NULL, B INTEGER CONSTRAINT PK PRIMARY KEY (TENANT\_ID, A));CREATE TABLE T2 (TENANT\_ID VARCHAR NOT NULL, A INTEGER NOT NULL, B INTEGER CONSTRAINT PK PRIMARY KEY (TENANT\_ID, A));CREATE VIEW V1 (NEW\_COL1 INTEGER, NEW\_COL2 INTEGER) AS SELECT \* FROM T1 WHERE B \> 10;CREATE VIEW V1 (NEW\_COL1 INTEGER, NEW\_COL2 INTEGER) AS SELECT \* FROM T2 WHERE B \> 10; |
| :---- |

Of course step 4 fails, but we still see the following when we query SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK:  
![][image1]  
There is an orphan linking row created between T2 and V1 though V1 is actually a view on top of T1. 

At this point, even if we were to drop the view V1, this orphan linking row still remains:

# What is the problem if these orphan rows exist?

## Wrong DDL behavior {#wrong-ddl-behavior}

Many DDL operations will wrongly fail due to the presence of these orphan linking rows. DDL operations identified which can fail due to orphan rows are:

1. During a CREATE TABLE/VIEW, we try to drop any views from the previous life of that table/view, however **we might end up dropping a legitimate view (with the same name)** which is on another table/view because of this (see the call to [ViewUtil.dropChildViews()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L1763)).  
2. Any ALTER TABLE ADD/DROP/SET calls on a base table T will fail if there are orphan links from T to some already dropped view. This happens because the call to [MetaDataEndpointImpl.findAllChildViews()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2142) from [MetaDataEndpointImpl.mutateColumn()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2592) fails with a TableNotFoundException.  
3. Any DROP TABLE/VIEW call without CASCADE will fail even though there are actually no child views since the orphan linking rows wrongly indicate that there are child views (see [MetaDataEndpointImpl.doDropTable()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2459-L2469)).  
4. During the upgrade path for UpgradeUtil.syncUpdateCacheFreqAllIndexes(), we will just ignore any orphan views (for ex, see [this](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/util/UpgradeUtil.java#L1368-L1374)), but the call to UpgradeUtil.upgradeTable() will fail with a TableNotFoundException for each orphan view.

## Other concerns

Apart from these DDL issues, other problems due to these orphan linking rows are that any **metadata consistency checks can be thrown off** and there will be **unnecessary extra storage** of orphan links. The presence of orphan links also makes it operationally difficult to restore a cluster back to its normal state in case of any corruptions in SYSTEM table data.

# What is the aim of PHOENIX-6142?

The only way to prevent the creation of such orphan linking rows is to maintain some sort of consistency between SYSTEM.CATALOG and SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK by means of either transactions or 2-phase commit approach ([PHOENIX-6141](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PHOENIX-6141) aims to solve this issue).

PHOENIX-6142 does **NOT** aim to prevent the creation of orphan linking rows. Instead, it aims at making DDL operations **resilient** to such orphan linking rows so as to prevent the issues mentioned in the [previous section](#wrong-ddl-behavior). It is aimed as a means to proceed until we develop a robust solution to PHOENIX-6141 and in no way aims at reducing the importance of PHOENIX-6141.

# Proposed solution

Overall, the idea is that for any linking row ‘A-\>V’ that we find keyed by parent table/view ‘A’ inside SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK/SYSTEM.CATALOG, we only conclude that ‘V’ is a valid child of ‘A’ if we can resolve ‘V’ and confirm that the parent schema name and parent table name in fact corresponds to that of ‘A’.

We will delve into each DDL path mentioned in the [previous section](#wrong-ddl-behavior) 1-by-1.

## CREATE TABLE/VIEW path

Before proceeding to create the table/view, we try to drop any child views it may have had from a previous life which are not yet dropped (perhaps because the task to drop those views has not run yet). This is done in the call to [ViewUtil.dropChildViews()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L1763), wherein we directly find all immediately related views keyed by the parent table/view name and [attempt to drop them](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/util/ViewUtil.java#L237).

Here we might end up dropping a legitimate view (with the same name) which is on another table/view. In order to avoid this, we will attempt to resolve the view without using the cache (PhoenixRuntime.getTableNoCache()). The expectation is that since this is a view whose ancestor has already been dropped, the getTableNoCache() call will fail with a TableNotFoundException. At this point we are safe to issue a dropTable() on the view. **If however we are able to successfully resolve the view, that means it is a legitimate view and we should ignore it.**

## ALTER TABLE ADD/DROP/SET

Alter table calls go to MetaDataEndpointImpl.mutateColumn() wherein we find all child views of the table (see the call to [MetaDataEndpointImpl.findAllChildViews()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2592)). This findAllChildViews() call gets the entire child view hierarchy (children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and so on) of the base table by issuing scans on SYSTEM.CHILD\_LINK/SYSTEM.CATALOG to look for parent-\>child links. Inside this API we also try to resolve each view (see [this](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2166)). 

The call to PhoenixRuntime.getTableNoCache() will obviously fail with a TableNotFoundException if there are orphan links keyed by the table or its descendant to some already dropped view. This in turn fails the ALTER TABLE call. 

**We will introduce a new ViewUtil API called ‘findAllDescendantViews()’** which will find all the descendant views of a given table or view in a depth-first fashion. Note that apart from scanning the parent-\>child links, we also validate each view by trying to resolve it. This API in turn returns a pair of 2 lists:

1. **List\<PTable\> of legitimate child views**: This means that we were able to resolve the view via PhoenixRuntime.getTableNoCache() and the view was confirmed to be a child. We confirm this by inspecting the PTable of the view and confirming the parent schema name and parent table name.  
2. **List\<TableInfo\> of orphan views**: This means that view resolution failed with a TableNotFoundException. Thus, we now catch this exception and add this view’s TableInfo object to the list of orphan views we have found while finding all descendants of the given table/view.

A **3rd case is a view which can be successfully resolved, but whose parent is different from the expectation** i.e. parent schema name and parent table name do not match the key of the parent-\>child linking row. This can happen if we do the exercise mentioned in the [section above](#how-can-an-orphan-linking-row-be-created?) followed by dropping and recreating V1 on top of table T1. At this point, based on the orphan linking row T2-\>V1, V1 is a view on top of T2, however resolving the PTable for V2 confirms that it is in fact a child view of T1 and hence should not be counted as a legitimate view of T2.

The new API ‘findAllDescendantViews()’ **prunes orphan branches and views that are legitimate children on top of other parents and thus only explores legitimate parent-\>child links for that parent**. Finally, inside MetaDataEndpointImpl.mutateColumn(), we will only consider the legitimate children to decide whether the parent table/view mutation is valid or not and thus orphan linking rows do not fail or wrongly disallow these mutations.

### Can a child view be concurrently created/dropped right after we have scanned the parent-\>child links, thus making the list of child views incomplete/incorrect?

Note that before issuing an alter table add/drop column we do a conditional write with a checkAndPut to SYSTEM.MUTEX for the key:

| \<schema name\>, \<physical table name\>, \<column name\> |
| :---- |

Similarly when doing an alter view add/drop column, this is done for the key:

| \<physical parent's schema name\>, \<physical parent's table name\>, \<column name\> |
| :---- |

When creating a view, a similar conditional write is done with a checkAndPut to SYSTEM.MUTEX for the key:

| \<physical parent's schema name\>, \<physical parent's table name\>, \<column name\> |
| :---- |

During view creation, such a checkAndPut is done for each column that the view references i.e. present in the view WHERE clause. This checkAndPut logic thus prevents a case where clients might try to simultaneously create a view dependent on a column that the base table ([PHOENIX-6124](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PHOENIX-6124) extends this condition to parent views as well) is dropping and any other such conflicting modifications with respect to specific columns.

We are however, still able to create a view dependent on unrelated columns simultaneously, for ex: The following can happen simultaneously, **however that should be harmless** since our base table alterations do not affect this view at all.

| ALTER TABLE T ADD C INTEGER;CREATE VIEW V\_NEW AS SELECT \* FROM T WHERE B \> 10; |
| :---- |

We are however, able to concurrently drop a view (since drop view code does not do any checkAndPut logic). At worst, this means we will overcount and may unnecessarily fail the ALTER operation on the parent. **This operation will succeed once re-run after the drop child view** command has gone through, so this poses **no problem.**

Thus, the current logic (unmodified in the PR for this Jira) ensures that the list of child views we get which are relevant to the base table column(s) being added/dropped **does not undercount/miss any child views which may be affected**.

## DROP TABLE/VIEW path

In the current implementation, inside MetaDataEndpointImpl.dropTable(), we acquire a row lock on the table/view header row (see [this](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2253)) and then inside MetaDataEndpointImpl.doDropTable(), we check if the table/view has any child views (see [this](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2455-L2501)). In case there are any orphan linking rows, say ‘T-\>V’ for a view ‘V’ that has already been dropped, the ‘DROP TABLE/VIEW T’ call without CASCADE will fail even though there are actually no child views on ‘T’ (see [MetaDataEndpointImpl.doDropTable()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2459-L2469)).

The main changes here are:

1. Move the [child views check logic](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2455-L2501) outside of doDropTable() and **before acquiring the row lock on the table/view header row**.   
   1. This has to be done since the calls to resolve the PTable for views using PhoenixRuntime.getTableNoCache() requires a write lock on the header row of the view’s parent.   
   2. If we were to do view resolution after acquiring the row lock for the table/view header row, **it would lead to a deadlock**.  
2. Instead of a simple scan to check for the presence of any child view via [ViewUtil.hasChildViews()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2460), we use the newly introduced ViewUtil.‘findAllDescendantViews() API (with a flag indicating that we just want to find 1 legitimate view). This ensures that the absence of CASCADE check is done only if there are legitimate views. Similarly, [this check](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/coprocessor/MetaDataEndpointImpl.java#L2488-L2498) for older clients connecting to non-upgraded servers is also only done if there are legitimate views.  
3. Finally, if the CASCADE option is provided and we have at least one legitimate/orphan view stemming from this parent and the client is 4.15+ (or older but connecting to an upgraded server), we use the SYSTEM.TASK table to asynchronously drop child views.

The reason why we include orphan views in the final step is that any view for which its parent hierarchy is already dropped will now be an orphan since its PTable resolution will fail with a TableNotFoundException. Since the DropChildViewsTask works level by level, we must continue dropping views and adding tasks for clearing their child views.

### Can a child view be concurrently created/dropped right after we have scanned the parent-\>child links, thus making the list of child views incomplete/incorrect? {#can-a-child-view-be-concurrently-created/dropped-right-after-we-have-scanned-the-parent->child-links,-thus-making-the-list-of-child-views-incomplete/incorrect?}

There is no checkAndPut logic to SYSTEM.MUTEX from the client-side in the DROP TABLE/VIEW code path. [PHOENIX-4875](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PHOENIX-4875) removed the code that acquired a mutex when dropping a table and creating a view. The idea is, even if a child view is being concurrently created and we miss accounting for it in the DROP TABLE/VIEW of its parent, **the next time we resolve this child view, it will throw a TableNotFoundException since one or more of its ancestors does not exist**. This is exactly what would happen if we tried to query a view whose parent has already been dropped and the view hasn’t been cleaned up via the DropChildViewsTask and is thus safe. 

### Can any other problems occur now that we have moved the logic to find child views before acquiring a write lock on the parent/view’s header row?

Currently (without this PR), since we acquire a row lock on the header row of the table/view we want to drop inside the dropTable code, view creation on top of this table/view is blocked since view resolution also tries to get its ancestors and this blocks on the row lock for the parent. The converse is also true i.e. dropTable can be blocked if child view creation gets the row lock on the parent first.

**This however is probably not necessary and in fact may be an unnecessary overhead**. The reason is similar to the explanation in the [previous section](#can-a-child-view-be-concurrently-created/dropped-right-after-we-have-scanned-the-parent-\>child-links,-thus-making-the-list-of-child-views-incomplete/incorrect?). 

After this PR, overall here are possible scenarios during a DROP TABLE/VIEW ‘A’ where ‘A’ is a parent of 0 or more views:

**Case 1: Drop Table/View \+ concurrent child view creation**

- If the view gets created before the dropTable code has accounted for all child views  
  - We will count this new child view, so **no problem**  
- If the view gets created after the dropTable code has accounted for all child views  
  - We will miss counting this new child view  
  - One of the following can occur:  
    - If CASCADE was provided and the parent has other views, we will have created a DropChildViewsTask for the parent, which when it gets picked up will also clear this new child view, so **no problem**  
    - If CASCADE was provided and the parent has no other views, we will not create a DropChildViewsTask for the parent and the dropTable goes through. Now whenever the new child view is resolved, it fails with a TableNotFoundException as expected since its parent doesn’t exist, so **no problem → This needs to be cleared up via the OrphanViewTool at this point**  
    - If CASCADE was not provided and the parent had other views, the dropTable call fails, so **no problem**  
    - If CASCADE was not provided and the parent had no other views, dropTable goes through. Now whenever the new child view is resolved, it fails with a TableNotFoundException as expected since its parent doesn’t exist, so **no problem → This needs to be cleared up via the OrphanViewTool at this point**

**Case 2: Drop Table/View  \+ concurrent child view drop**

- If the view gets dropped before the dropTable code has accounted for all child views  
  - We will not count this child view as expected, so **no problem**  
- If the view gets dropped after the dropTable code has accounted for all child views  
  - We will unnecessarily count this child view  
  - One of the following can occur:  
    - If CASCADE was provided and the parent has other views, we will have created a DropChildViewsTask for the parent, so when it gets picked up, even if the view doesn’t exist anymore, the DROP VIEW command will fail silently, so **no problem**  
    - If CASCADE was provided and the parent has no other views, we will still create a DropChildViewsTask for the parent since this child views still exists, so when the task gets picked up, even if the view doesn’t exist anymore, the DROP VIEW command will fail silently, so **no problem**  
    - If CASCADE was not provided and the parent had other views, the dropTable call fails, so **no problem**  
    - If CASCADE was not provided and the parent had no other views, the dropTable call fails since the child view still exists. This will pass if re-run once the child view drop command goes through, so **no problem**

## Metadata upgrade path

The changes in this path are to fail silently in case we fail to resolve a view. We are already doing this in other upgrade code like [UpgradeUtil.syncUpdateCacheFreqAllIndexes()](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/util/UpgradeUtil.java#L1370-L1374) and we must extend this to UpgradeUtil.mapChildViewsToNamespace() ([here](https://github.com/apache/phoenix/blob/fece8e69b9c03c80db7a0801d99e5de31fe15ffa/phoenix-core/src/main/java/org/apache/phoenix/util/UpgradeUtil.java#L2325)) where we iterate over viewInfo based on parent-\>child links.
